scope_basis: Loan to a fibre network operator for refinancing and network maintenance.
title: EAIF — Liquid Intelligent Technologies pan-African fibre refinancing, 2026
description:
Verbatim from the financier's own release:

> EAAIF has also committed USD 50 million to Liquid Intelligent Technologies as part of a USD 450 million restructuring and expansion package. This investment supports the optimisation of Liquid's capital structure and the maintenance of its 110,000 km cross-border fibre network across 25 countries, including Kenya, South Africa and Zimbabwe.

> This network is key for Africa's digital data storage and processing, serving major operators, enterprises, and hyperscalers. By investing in Liquid's high-speed broadband and cloud infrastructure, EAAIF reinforces its commitment to sovereign digital assets that drive economic growth.

> EAAIF's green covenants also align with Liquid Intelligent Technologies' parent company, Cassava Technologies, in its transition path to achieve a 42% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030.

scope_basis: Stake in a venture fund for technology start-ups.
title: African Development Bank Group — Saviu II fund, 2026
description: "The African Development Bank Group is investing 6.5 million euro stake in the Saviu II fund to support technology start-ups in French-speaking Africa." "The Bank Group will invest 4.5 million euros as equity and 2 million euros as a first-loss hedging tranche on behalf of the European Commission, under the Boost Africa Programme." "The Saviu II venture capital fund aims to make at least 60% of its commitments in the French-speaking countries of West and Central Africa: Côte d'Ivoire, Cameroon, Benin, Senegal, Togo, Burkina Faso and Mali." "Saviu II... plans to invest between 500,000 and three million euros in about 20 technology or technology-oriented B2B start-ups in the seed phase or carrying out first institutional fundraising."

Initial deployments: (i) USD 25 million anchor commitment to Lightrock Africa Fund II (Lightrock portfolio includes Moniepoint, Lula, M-KOPA); (ii) USD 15 million to Future Africa Fund III (early-stage venture capital backing technology-enabled solutions). The remaining USD 60 million is earmarked for additional fund managers under evaluation. Sectors covered: fintech, digital infrastructure, consumer technology, education technology. The commitment represents AFC's strategic entry into Africa's venture capital ecosystem to mobilise institutional capital and deepen African ownership of tech investment.
recipient_organisation: Lightrock Africa Fund II / Future Africa Fund III

scope_basis: Loan to a telecom operator to expand 4G, 5G and fibre networks.
title: EBRD — Yas Kenya/Senegal network expansion, 2026
description:
"The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is providing a senior loan of up to €270 million to pan-African telecoms operator Yas to fund network expansion in Senegal and Kenya." "The deal marks the EBRD's first investment in Senegal and its first local-currency financing and A/B loan structure in sub-Saharan Africa." "The committed facility totals up to €170 million, split between a €100 million EBRD A-loan, a B-loan of up to €50 million to be syndicated to institutional investors, and a local-currency facility of up to €20 million equivalent in Kenyan shillings. Amsterdam-based impact private credit fund ILX Fund will take a sizeable position in the B-loan. A further uncommitted facility of up to €100 million is available for future Yas acquisitions and capital expenditure." "Yas, owned by AXIAN Telecom, will use the funding to expand 4G, 5G and fibre infrastructure across both markets." In Kenya the capital modernises the Zuku fibre network (Yas acquired Zuku's parent Wananchi Group in 2025).

Recipient countries: KEN, SEN.
original_amount: EUR up to 170,000,000 committed (€100m EBRD A-loan + up to €50m B-loan + up to €20m KES-equivalent local currency; up to €270m headline including a further up to €100m uncommitted facility)

scope_basis: Loan funds submarine capacity, data centres and fibre.
title: IFC — WIOCC Group sustainability-linked loan (WIOCC VI Debt), 2025
description:
Verbatim from IFC's Environmental & Social Review Summary for project 51154:

> IFC’s proposed financing package includes an equity investment of up to US$50 million and a sustainability-linked loan of up to US$20.4 million equivalent (a US$10 million tranche and a South African Rand tranche of US$10.4 million equivalent). The project’s principal activities include: (a) acquiring capacity from existing submarine cables, (b) expanding data centre infrastructure, (c) growing the new fiber-to-the-home/business (FTTx), and (d) investing in terrestrial fibre. Key efforts are focused on increasing data centre capacity in South Africa and Nigeria through the construction of a new block at the Lagos (Lekki) Data Centre and the expansion of the current facility in Durban.

Verbatim from IFC's Summary of Investment Information for the same project:

> The proposed IFC investment comprises a senior secured sustainability-linked loan (“SLF”) of up to US$20.8 mn to WIOCC’s subsidiaries: WIOCC Mauritius (“WIOCC MU”) (US$ loan) and OADC PropCo South Africa (“OADC SA”) (ZAR loan), jointly referred to as “WIOCC Group”.

> This current project is considered an extension of WIOCC SLF loan (#48053) and OADC SLF Loan (#49887) which also sought to enhance connectivity and data hosting services for individuals and businesses in Africa.

Project events as disclosed by IFC: Approved 5 December 2025; Signed 10 December 2025; Invested 14 May 2026.
original_amount: US$10 million tranche plus a South African rand tranche of US$10.4 million equivalent (the rand sum is not stated)

scope_basis: GPU-equipped data-centre capacity for AI across five hubs.
title: Cassava Technologies — NVIDIA AI factory, Africa's first: US$720m programme announced 2025
description: Cassava Technologies announced on 24 March 2025 that it plans to build Africa's first AI factory — a data-centre facility powered by NVIDIA accelerated computing, deployed using NVIDIA Cloud Partner reference architectures. Strive Masiyiwa, founder and chairman, framed it as infrastructure for the AI economy that keeps data within Africa's borders; Jaap Zuiderveld, NVIDIA VP EMEA, confirmed the NCP partnership. Cassava committed to deploy at its South African data centres **by June 2025**, with expansion planned to its facilities in **Egypt, Kenya, Morocco and Nigeria**. On 7 April 2025 Bloomberg reported the programme's cost at **US$720 million**, covering roughly 12,000 NVIDIA GPUs across five regional hubs over three to four years. The South Africa hub went live in November 2025. In October 2025 NVIDIA took an equity stake in Cassava (amount undisclosed) as part of a US$150m+ equity raise for Liquid Intelligent Technologies, and STANLIB agreed a minority stake in Africa Data Centres. Primary sub-Saharan countries are ZAF, NGA and KEN; Egypt and Morocco are outside SSA.

scope_basis: Guarantee covers investments in data centres.
title: MIGA — Raxio Group data centres political risk guarantee (Meridiam master contract), 2022
description:
Verbatim from MIGA's Summary of Proposed Guarantee:

> This summary covers an application made by Meridiam Africa Investments 2 SAS (Meridiam), a global developer, investor and asset manager specializing in public and community infrastructure, for MIGA to provide a programmatic Master Contract (MC) covering its investments alongside the Roha Group in Data Center projects in East, West, and Southern Africa, through Raxio Group BV (Raxio). The duration of the MC would be for up to 4 years, during which Meridiam could request MIGA cover for the different subprojects.

> MIGA's political risk insurance (PRI) has been requested against the risks of Expropriation, Transfer Restriction, and War & Civil Disturbance for the first batch of three subprojects, located in Mozambique, Uganda and Cote d'Ivoire (the Host Countries). MIGA guarantees would be provided in the aggregate amount of up to US$11.01 million for a period of up to 15 years.

> The project involves the design, finance, construction and O&M of a series of "metro edge" Data Centers, each of which would deliver approximately 1 to 1.5 MW of IT power. The Data Centers are expected to be fully redundant and able to operate independently of the power grid for extended periods of time, and do not require any shutdown when equipment needs maintenance or replacement.

> The Project is a category B project under MIGA's Policy on Environmental and Social Sustainability.

> The Project's development impact will be driven by key investments in private sector-driven data hosting solutions across the three Host Countries. The Project will support the development of the local digital industry and promote digital connectivity, by increasing access to a critical digital infrastructure (data centers). The Project also has potential to facilitate the expansion of innovation and competition of the domestic digital market and the wider service delivery of web services in Africa.

> The project is consistent with the WBG Digital Economy for Africa Initiative (DE4A) and the African Union (AU) Digital Transformation Strategy for Africa, which aims to ensure that every African individual, business, and government will be digitally enabled by 2030. The Project will also support MIGA's objective of expanding its footprint and deepening impact in IDA/FCS countries, based on the recognition that the private sector is the primary creator of jobs and growth. The Project is also aligned with the IDA-20 commitments to expanding broadband usage for jobs of the future and positioning more firms for recovery through the adaptation of digital technology.
recipient_organisation: Raxio Group BV, via Meridiam Africa Investments 2 SAS as guarantee holder
original_amount: US$11.01 million (aggregate, first batch of three subprojects)

Portfolio countries include Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa (DRC, Ethiopia, Côte d'Ivoire per DFC filing). Fund size ~USD 250M+ with co-investors including EIB, DFC, Finnfund.

financier: Belgian Investment Company for Developing Countries
scope_basis: Equity in a credit fund that lends to fintech companies.
title: Lendable MSME Fintech Credit Fund — Equity Commitment
description: USD 5M equity in Lendable MSME FinTech Credit Fund I, a closed-end private credit fund providing debt financing to fintech companies across Africa and Asia. BIO invested USD 4M equity in 2022 (following a loan in 2020). Lendable finances fintechs enabling consumer/MSME credit, productive asset finance, payments, remittances, and digital marketplaces. SSA beneficiary countries: Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa (also Liberia, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, Uganda per related investments).

scope_basis: Programme builds digital skills in formal and non-formal education.
title: GenerationDigital! GenerationDigital!
description: Context:   Digital skills are a basic necessity for internet-based participation in society and politics, greater employability and the critical use of new media. Both the formal and non-formal (out-of-school) education systems play a special role in this context. Classical learning formats are increasingly being complemented, expanded or even replaced by digital formats. However, the education systems in many states, including in some African countries, are unable to keep pace with technologica

scope_basis: Bond of a telecom group, used for new mobile antennas and digital infrastructure.
title: DEG Anchor Investment in AXIAN Telecom USD 420M Bond (2022)
description: DEG invests USD 23 million as anchor investor in AXIAN Telecom's debut USD 420 million bond (7.375% senior notes due 2027). AXIAN Telecom is a pan-African telecommunications group operating in Tanzania (including Tigo Tanzania acquisition), Madagascar, Togo, Senegal, and Uganda. The bond proceeds are used to install approximately 1,250 new mobile-phone antennas, improve digital infrastructure and liquidity for future investments. Four DFI anchor investors: CDC Group (USD 30M), DEG (USD 23M), Emerging Africa Infrastructure Fund (EAIF), and IFC (USD 50M).

scope_basis: Equity in an e-commerce company with digital financial services.
title: DEG Equity Investment in Copia Global E-Commerce and Fintech (2022)
description: DEG provides USD 7.5 million in equity capital to Copia Global Inc., a pan-African e-commerce company operating in Kenya and Uganda. Copia enables low- and middle-income consumers in East Africa to access a wide range of products through a network of agents using a digital platform. Over the past year, Copia expanded to include integrated FinTech services such as operating loans for Copia Agents, managed through a digital channel. Proceeds grow core business, fund pan-African expansion, and develop integrated financial services. Total round approximately USD 50 million. Co-investors include DFC, Goodwell Investments, Lightrock, and Zebu Investment Partners.

scope_basis: Equity in a growth-stage technology fund.
title: Norrsken22 Africa Tech Growth Fund — DFC $15M Equity
description: DFC equity investment of up to $15 million in Norrsken22 Africa Tech Growth Fund, a women-led pan-African growth-stage technology fund investing in fintech, edtech, health tech, and market-enabling solutions across sub-Saharan Africa. Fund achieved final close at $205M. Portfolio companies include TymeBank (digital challenger bank), Smile Identity (identity verification), Autochek (auto financing), Sabi (B2B commerce platform), Shara (merchant financing). DFC is an anchor impact investor.

financier: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands
scope_basis: Fund described wholly as mobile and technology platforms connecting health service demand and supply.
title: Health Innovation Fund Partnership 2023-2029 Mobile Health Technology Africa
description: Partnership renewal for the Health Innovation Fund (HIF) for 2023-2029. HIF improves healthcare markets through mobile and technology innovations in Africa. Mission: making inclusive health markets work. Uses mobile platforms to connect health service demand and supply at scale.

scope_basis: Investment in mobile money services.
title: Moov Africa Mobile Money Platform Investment Across SSA
description: Maroc Telecom has invested in mobile money services through its Moov Africa brand across SSA. Mobile Money revenues grew 14.4% in 2024. The IFC EUR 375 million loan (2023) to Moov Africa subsidiaries in 8 SSA countries includes funding for mobile money and digital financial services alongside network capex. Countries: Benin, Burkina Faso, Chad, Côte d'Ivoire, Gabon, Mali, Niger, Togo.

scope_basis: Investment in a transafrican terrestrial fibre cable.
title: Maroc Telecom Transafrican Terrestrial Fibre Cable - Landlocked SSA Connectivity
description: Maroc Telecom invested in a 5,700 km transafrican terrestrial cable connecting Morocco to Niger via Mauritania, Mali, and Burkina Faso, as part of MAD 2 billion+ invested in transafrican connectivity infrastructure. This cable enables the landlocked Moov Africa subsidiaries in Mauritania, Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger to connect to international bandwidth via the Maroc Telecom network. Investment disclosed as part of Maroc Telecom's 2024 reporting.

scope_basis: Contract deploys a digital traceability and verification system for vaccines and health products.
title: Supporting the implementation of the Traceability and Verification System (TrVsT) for COVID-19 vaccines and other health products
description: Contract related to: Supporting the implementation of the Traceability and Verification System (TrVsT) for COVID-19 vaccines and other health products - Support to the deployment of digital health tools for COVID-19 tools deployment in Sub-Saharan Africa

scope_basis: Equity in a venture fund for digital and technology start-ups.
title: PARTECH AFRICA VENTURE CAPITAL FUND II
description: Equity participation in Partech Africa II, a EUR 230M venture capital fund focusing on start-ups and high-growth SMEs active in digital and technology sectors in Africa. Fund targets local start-ups in digital/tech sectors across Africa. EIB committed EUR 20M as anchor investor. Co-investors include KfW, IFC, FMO, BII, DEG, Bpifrance. Successor to Partech Africa Fund I.

scope_basis: Programme improves cybersecurity capability, data protection and digital forensics.
title: Africa Cyber Programme (ACP)
description: FCDO programme investing £3 million over 16 months (October 2022 to March 2024) to improve cybersecurity capability and reduce cyber harm in Kenya, Nigeria and South Africa. Funded from the Conflict, Stability and Security Fund (CSSF). Builds on the DAP Pillar 2 Trust and Resilience cybersecurity investment. Delivered by KPMG, implementing 6 projects including: supporting government data protection capability in Kenya; strengthening Nigeria's law enforcement digital forensic capability; improving South Africa police ability to prosecute cyber criminals. Contributes to UK vision of thriving, open digital societies powered by trusted technologies.
recipient_organisation: Governments/implementing partners in Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa

scope_basis: Commitment to a digital infrastructure fund.
title: Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund (CPDIF)
description: Finnfund committed USD 15 million to the Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund, a USD 296 million fund investing in digital infrastructure and digital services across Sub-Saharan Africa. Portfolio includes fibre networks, data centres, cloud platforms and telecom infrastructure operators across multiple SSA countries.
recipient_organisation: Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund LP

scope_basis: Loan to a mobile money platform.
title: Wave Mobile Money SSA Expansion
description: Finnfund EUR 12 million parallel loan to Wave Mobile Money, a low-cost mobile money platform providing affordable deposit, withdrawal and payment services in West Africa. Wave operates in LDC countries with very low banking penetration, offering free deposit/withdrawal services to increase financial inclusion.
recipient_organisation: Wave Mobile Money S.A. / Wave Côte d'Ivoire S.A.

scope_basis: Commitment to a venture fund that invests only in tech start-ups.
title: Partech Africa Fund II SSA Tech Startup VC Fund
description: FMO equity commitment of EUR 25M to Partech Africa Fund II, a generalist tech venture capital fund targeting early-stage fintech, mobile consumer services, mobility, supply chain, and digital economy startups in Sub-Saharan Africa. Fund closed at EUR 263M/USD 300M+ with KfW as anchor.

scope_basis: Deployment of a regional instant digital payment system.
title: COMESA MSME focused Digital Real Time Retail Payment Platform (Phase III)
description: this investment will be used to support the COMESA Business Council to deploy a pro-poor instant and inclusive digital payment system and  scheme rules/standards that will serve the payment needs of MSME's in COMESA region in Africa

scope_basis: Bond of a telecoms group financing network expansion, spectrum and mobile money.
title: Axian Telecom Bond — IFC Anchor Investor
description: IFC acted as anchor investor in Axian Telecom's debut bond issuance, committing $60 million from its own account. Axian Telecom is a pan-African telecommunications and digital infrastructure company operating in Madagascar, Tanzania, Togo, Senegal, Comoros, and Réunion. The bond — total size approximately €430 million — finances network expansion, spectrum acquisition, and mobile money infrastructure across Axian's SSA markets. IFC's anchor participation was intended to attract market investors at a time of financial market volatility. BII and other DFIs co-participated.

scope_basis: Loan to a mobile operator for 4G rollout and network upgrades.
title: Airtel Africa Mobile Internet Connectivity Expansion (2022)
description: IFC committed $150 million from its own account plus $44 million from the Managed Co-Lending Portfolio Program (MCPP) — a total of $194 million — to Airtel Africa to support expansion of mobile internet connectivity across six Sub-Saharan African countries: DRC, Kenya, Madagascar, Niger, Republic of Congo, and Zambia. Airtel Africa is one of the continent's leading mobile network operators. The financing enables rollout of 4G networks, upgrading of existing infrastructure, and expansion into underserved rural and peri-urban areas, directly contributing to affordable mobile internet access for millions of users.

scope_basis: Equity for data centres and fibre networks.
title: WIOCC Group Equity Investment — Data Centres and Fibre (2022)
description: IFC made a $30 million equity investment in WIOCC Holding Company Ltd (WHCL), the restructured parent of WIOCC, to support expansion of core and edge data centres and fibre networks in DRC, Nigeria, and South Africa. WIOCC's Open Access Data Centres (OADC) strategy targets Tier III data centres across Africa serving cloud providers, enterprises, and internet exchanges. The IFC equity stake aligns with WIOCC's $200M combined debt and equity raise in 2021-2022 to fund the OADC strategy. Proparco, EAAIF (Ninety-One), and other DFIs also participated.
recipient_organisation: WIOCC Group (WIOCC Holding Company Ltd / Open Access Data Centres)

scope_basis: Debt facility to a mobile money company.
title: Wave Mobile Money — IFC Debt Facility (Senegal + Côte d'Ivoire)
description: IFC provided a senior debt facility of €25 million (A-loan) to Wave Mobile Money S.A. (Senegal entity) and Wave Côte d'Ivoire S.A. as part of a €130 million total financing package. Wave is Francophone Africa's first fintech unicorn ($1.7B valuation), operating a low-cost interoperable mobile money platform across Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Burkina Faso, Gambia, Mali, Niger, and Uganda. IFC's participation mobilised €65M in B-loans from impact lenders (Symbiotics, BlueOrchard, responsAbility, Lendable). Proparco/Finnfund/Norfund provided €24M in parallel loans. Total €130M package.
recipient_organisation: Wave Mobile Money S.A. (Senegal) / Wave Côte d'Ivoire S.A.

scope_basis: Lender finances smartphones and digital financial services but also solar home systems, which are not digital.
title: M-KOPA Connected Asset Financing — IFC Senior Debt Facility
description: IFC committed senior secured loans to M-KOPA: up to $50 million (or KES equivalent) to M-KOPA Kenya Limited and up to $15 million (or UGX equivalent) to M-KOPA Uganda Limited. M-KOPA is Africa's leading connected asset financing provider, offering smartphones, solar home systems, and digital financial services (cash loans, mobile insurance) to over-indebted, underserved households through a pay-as-you-go (PAYG) model using mobile money instalments. Approved December 2022 and invested February 2023. IFC is a principal debt financier alongside BII which also holds equity and debt positions.
recipient_organisation: M-KOPA Kenya Limited / M-KOPA Uganda Limited

scope_basis: Commitment to a venture fund investing in technology businesses.
title: Partech Africa Fund II — IFC LP Commitment
description: IFC committed up to €25 million (~$26.3M) as a limited partner in Partech Africa Fund II (PAF II), an early-stage venture capital fund investing in Seed to Series D technology businesses across Africa. Partech Africa II reached final close above €300 million in 2024. Co-LPs include BII ($15.6M), KfW, EIB, DEG, FMO, Proparco, Mubadala, and Bpifrance. The fund targets fintech, logistics, digital health, e-commerce, and digital infrastructure companies. Portfolio includes Wave (mobile money), Maad Africa, Revio Pay, Foondamate, and others across 27+ African countries.

scope_basis: Fund for digital transformation of public administrations.
title: Fonds für Digitale Transformation Westafrika
description: Die öffentlichen Verwaltungen Westafrikas haben einen hohen Modernisierungsbedarf, um die SDGs zu erreichen. Denn eine zentrale Voraussetzung zur Verbesserung der Regierungsführung in Afrika ist deren digitale Transformation: Durch die Digitalisierung der Verwaltung und Automatisierung ihrer Prozesse können die Kosten reduziert, Effizienz und Transparenz erhöht werden. Eine digitale Verwaltung kann damit entscheidend dazu beitragen, die Korruption zu senken und die Rechenschaftspflicht der Regie

scope_basis: Commitment to a venture fund investing in tech start-ups.
title: AfricaGrow LP commitment to TLcom TIDE Africa Fund II
description: AfricaGrow (through Allianz and DEG Impact joint vehicle) commits to TLcom Capital's TIDE Africa Fund II, Africa's largest early-stage VC fund at $154M final close. Fund targets seed and Series A across East and West Africa (Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt, South Africa). Digital focus: fintech, agritech, healthtech, logistics. First close $70M in Jan 2022, final close April 2024.

scope_basis: Loan to a pure-play mobile money company.
title: Wave Mobile Money — EUR 90M Syndicated Debt Facility
description: Norfund EUR 12 million parallel bilateral loan in EUR 90 million IFC-led syndicated debt facility for Wave Mobile Money. Wave provides low-cost mobile wallet, transfers, and merchant payment services in Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Gambia, Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger. Pure-play mobile money unicorn in Francophone West Africa. Digital scope: mobile money platform, digital payments, financial inclusion.

scope_basis: Operator network capital expenditure on 4G, 5G and fibre.
title: Orange MEA Annual Network CapEx Programme 2022 (SSA portion)
description: Orange invested over €1 billion in 2022 across its MEA region for network deployment including 4G/5G rollout, fibre extension, and mobile broadband across SSA countries including Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, Cameroon, Mali, Burkina Faso, Guinea, Madagascar, DRC, Liberia, Sierra Leone.

scope_basis: Bond investment in a telecom group for telecom expansion.
title: Axian Telecom Bond - EAIF Anchor Investment
description: EAIF was an anchor investor in bond issuances by Axian Telecom, a pan-African telecommunications and digital company. First investment: USD 20M in the February 2022 bond (total USD 420M raised) to fund telecom expansion. Second tranche: USD 30M commitment in 2023 bond. Axian operates in Madagascar, Togo, Tanzania, Uganda, Senegal, Comoros and other markets.

scope_basis: Fund finances digital financial infrastructure, agent networks and mobile money platforms.
title: Accion Digital Transformation Fund (Africa fintech)
description: Accion Digital Transformation Fund 2022-2032, a private debt impact investment fund providing finance to financial institutions and fintech companies in Africa. Supports digital financial infrastructure, agent networks and mobile money platforms to expand access to formal financial services for underserved populations across sub-Saharan Africa.

scope_basis: Phase-out support for an ICT capacity programme.
title: SPIDER Phase-out Support 2022-2024
description: Phase-out support for SPIDER (Swedish Programme for ICT in Developing Regions) at Stockholm University covering 2022-2024. SSA countries include Kenya, Uganda, South Africa and Zambia. Supports knowledge transfer and closure activities for the long-running ICT capacity programme.

scope_basis: Commitment to a venture fund investing in tech companies.
title: Cathay AfricInvest Innovation Fund I — SIFEM
description: SIFEM committed EUR 7 million to Cathay AfricInvest Innovation Fund I (CAIF I), a €110 million pan-African venture capital fund jointly managed by AfricInvest and Cathay Innovation. The fund invests in innovative African tech companies across software, financial services, communications, healthcare and education, supporting digital entrepreneurship and financial innovation across SSA.
recipient_organisation: Cathay AfricInvest Innovation Fund I (CAIF I)

scope_basis: Commitment to a fund investing in fibre, data centres, cloud and telecom platforms.
title: Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund (CPDIF) — SIFEM
description: SIFEM committed USD 15 million to the Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund (CPDIF), a USD 296 million fund investing in digital infrastructure and digital services companies across Sub-Saharan Africa. The fund bridges the digital divide in SSA by investing in fibre networks, data centres, cloud infrastructure and telecom platforms.
recipient_organisation: Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund LP

scope_basis: Commitment to a fund lending only to fintech companies.
title: Lendable MSME Fintech Credit Fund — SIFEM
description: SIFEM committed USD 10 million to the Lendable MSME Fintech Credit Fund, a USD 110 million fintech debt fund providing senior-secured debt to early and mid-stage fintech companies across Africa and Asia. The fund supports digital financial inclusion by enabling fintech lenders providing consumer and MSME credit, payments, and remittances to underbanked populations in Africa.

scope_basis: Fund whose stated purpose is the digital transformation of financial institutions.
title: Accion Digital Transformation Fund
description: Swedfund invested up to USD 15 million in the Accion Digital Transformation Fund, focused on the digital transformation of financial institutions in developing countries in Africa and South and Southeast Asia. Accion supports digital transformation through capital, strategic and technical advice and governance support to microfinance institutions and financial service providers. The fund raised USD 152.5 million in its 2024 close with co-investors BII, FMO, IFC, Mastercard, and OeEB.

scope_basis: Commitment to a venture fund for digital businesses.
title: TIDE Africa Fund II
description: Swedfund invested USD 10 million in TIDE Africa Fund II, a venture capital fund by TLcom Capital dedicated to financing scalable and innovative digital business models in Africa. The fund supports tech entrepreneurs building digital solutions from local needs in Africa, contributing to increased digitalisation, digital inclusion and economic growth. Portfolio companies operate in Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt and South Africa.

scope_basis: Investment in a data centre developer to deploy data centres.
title: Meridiam — Raxio Data Centres, 2021
description:
"The Raxio Group (“Raxio”), a premier pan-African data centre developer and operator, and Meridiam, a global developer, asset and fund manager specialising in sustainable infrastructure and energy transition projects today announced a partnership to deploy a network of data centres across the African continent. Under this agreement, Meridiam will invest $48 million to support the continued deployment of data centres in Africa, where both Raxio and Meridiam already have strong local presence. Meridiam’s investment is made alongside Raxio’s founding equity partner, Roha Group who established Raxio in 2018, and has been funding the company since inception." (Meridiam, 29 March 2021.)

Raxio's operating geography at the announcement, in its CEO's words: a first flagship facility in **Uganda**, construction launched in **Ethiopia**, and investment in a third facility in the **Democratic Republic of Congo**. The record takes the smallest covering region, XSS, since Uganda and Ethiopia (XEA) and the DRC (XCA) sit in different sub-regions.

scope_basis: Programme to build ten data centres.
title: Africa Data Centres — $500 Million Pan-African Data Centre Build-Out Programme
description: In September 2021, Africa Data Centres (ADC), a subsidiary of Cassava Technologies (formerly Liquid Intelligent Technologies), announced a $500 million investment programme to build 10 interconnected, cloud- and carrier-neutral data centres across 10 African countries over two years, doubling its existing footprint. The programme is financed through a combination of debt and equity, including a $300 million DFC direct loan (committed 2020, first disbursement Aug 2022 for South Africa), corporate equity from Cassava Technologies/ADC, and local debt facilities. Target countries include South Africa (Johannesburg JHB1, JHB2, Cape Town CPT1, CPT2), Kenya (Nairobi NBO1, NBO2), Nigeria (Lagos LOS1), Ghana (Accra ACC1), Togo (Lomé), and others. As of 2024, ADC has spent the $500M and operates facilities from South Africa to West Africa.

scope_basis: Equity in a telecoms tower developer.
title: Eastcastle Infrastructure — Consortium Equity Investment (Adenia Stake)
description: Adenia Partners, together with African Infrastructure Investment Managers (AIIM) and IFC, invested a total of USD 130 million in Eastcastle Infrastructure Limited, a newly established telecom tower developer in Africa. Eastcastle was founded in 2020 by former Eaton Towers CFO and COO. The consortium holds 95.8% of Eastcastle (AIIM 37.9%, Adenia 37.9%, IFC 20%, founders 4.2%). Funds support a build-to-suit strategy to develop new telecom towers for 3G/4G/5G deployment in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Nigeria, and Côte d'Ivoire. Adenia's committed share is approximately $49.3 million (37.9% of $130M total).

scope_basis: Project supports digital payments and e-commerce policies.
title: Multinational - Institutional Support for Digital Payments and e-Commerce Policies for Cross-Border Trade (IDECT)
description: The proposed project is an institutional Support for Digital Payments and e-Commerce Policies for Cross-border Trade (IDECT). It will be financed with an ADF-15 Regional Public Good grant and the Executing Agency is the Smart Africa Secretariat. This project proposes to address key policy gaps to un...

scope_basis: Grant funds research and development in ICT cybersecurity, fintech and digital financial services.
title: Multinational - ICT Cybersecurity (R&D, FINTECH and DFS)
description: A grant of UA 1,503,895 (approximately USD 2,166,000) from ADFI for research and development in ICT cybersecurity, fintech, and digital financial services. Approved February 2021. Aimed at building cybersecurity capacity for digital financial services ecosystem in Africa.

scope_basis: Equity in a digital infrastructure company, partly to fund its open-access data centres.
title: African Capital Alliance (CAPE IV) — WIOCC Holding equity, 2021
description:
Verbatim from the adviser's own post:

> Verdant Capital has successfully advised WIOCC Holding Company Limited (WIOCC) in raising USD 124 million in equity capital. Of this, USD 75 million was invested by CAPE IV, a fund managed by African Capital Alliance, a leading African private equity fund manager. Additionally, USD 30 million was invested by the International Finance Corporation (IFC) in a follow-up round. The remaining balance was contributed by management and existing shareholders.

> A portion of the capital will be allocated to funding OADC, which is developing a transformative, interconnected network of open-access, carrier-neutral data centres across Africa. The initial phase includes data centres at key submarine cable landings in Lagos, Durban, and Mogadishu, enabling direct landing of international submarine capacity into carrier-neutral facilities.
original_amount: USD 75 million (the announcing party's own currency)

scope_basis: Financing round for a digital payments network.
title: AfricInvest FIVE co-leads $100M Series C for MFS Africa pan-African digital payments network
description: AfricInvest's Financial Inclusion Vehicle (FIVE) co-leads a USD 100 million Series C financing round (USD 70M equity + USD 30M debt) for MFS Africa, Africa's largest digital payments network and interoperability hub. Round co-led with existing investors Goodwell Investments and LUN Partners, alongside CommerzVentures, Allan Gray Ventures and Endeavour. MFS Africa connects mobile network operators across 40+ African markets through a single API, enabling mobile money interoperability and cross-border digital payments. AfricInvest also participated in the USD 100M Series C extension in 2022.

scope_basis: Commitment to a fund investing in data centres, fibre, broadband and tech-enabled services.
title: Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund — LP Investment
description: BII committed $40M total to the Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund (CPDIF), a specialist SSA digital infrastructure fund managed by Convergence Partners. Investment 1: $30M (Jul 2021). Investment 2: $10M top-up (Jun 2022). The fund invests in digital infrastructure across Sub-Saharan Africa including data centres, fibre networks, broadband connectivity, and tech-enabled services. Portfolio companies include: 42Markets (SA digital trading), C Squared InvestCo (fibre/data Mauritius), CTrack Africa (fleet telematics), Datacentrix (data centre SA), Merit HoldCo (Nigeria digital infrastructure), Yellow Digital Retailers (device financing: Madagascar, Malawi, Rwanda, Uganda, Zambia).

financier: Belgian Investment Company for Developing Countries
scope_basis: Equity in a venture fund investing in digital tech companies.
title: Cathay Africinvest Innovation Fund — Pan-African Venture Capital
description: EUR 6M (two tranches: EUR 4M in 2021 + EUR 2M follow-on) equity in Cathay AfricInvest Innovation Fund (CAIF), a pan-African VC fund. CAIF reached €110M final close in 2023, co-managed by AfricInvest and Cathay Innovation. Invests in digital tech companies from seed to growth stage across Africa (Egypt, Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa). Focus on digital economy, fintech, healthtech, edtech, and agritech startups with scaling potential.

scope_basis: Bond investment in a fibre and data centre group.
title: DEG Anchor Investment in Liquid Telecommunications USD 620M Bond (2021)
description: DEG invests USD 25 million as anchor investor in the USD 620 million bond issued by Liquid Telecommunications Financing PLC, part of the pan-African telecoms group Liquid Intelligent Technologies (owned by Econet Global). The bond was the first Liquid Telecom capital market issuance since 2017 and was oversubscribed 5x. Liquid Telecommunications operates Africa's largest multi-country fibre optic network across Sub-Saharan Africa including South Africa, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Kenya, Tanzania, DRC, and Botswana, also operating Africa Data Centres (ADC) as a subsidiary. Proceeds used to refinance existing debt and fund growth including new fibre infrastructure, data centres, and new technologies.
recipient_organisation: Liquid Telecommunications Holdings / Liquid Intelligent Technologies

scope_basis: Equity in a fund investing only in digital infrastructure.
title: Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund — DFC $25M Equity
description: DFC equity investment of up to $25 million in Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund (CPDIF), a specialist Africa-focused ICT private equity fund. The fund invests in optical fibre installations, wireless towers, data centres, cloud, IoT, and AI infrastructure across sub-Saharan Africa. First close July 2021 at $120M; final close $296M. Portfolio companies include CSquared (Kenya broadband). DFC share is up to $25M out of $296M fund. Target countries: DRC, Ethiopia, Côte d'Ivoire, Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, South Africa.
recipient_organisation: Convergence Partners Digital Infrastructure Fund L.P. / Convergence Partners Africa

scope_basis: Loan to a fund lending only to fintech companies.
title: Lendable MSME Fintech Credit Fund — DFC $20M Loan
description: DFC direct loan of up to $20 million to Lendable Fintech Credit Fund (Luxembourg RAIF), providing senior-secured debt facilities to early and mid-stage fintech companies operating in Africa (Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa, Senegal) and Asia. Lendable's data-driven approach enables on-lending to digital financial service providers serving underbanked MSMEs. DFC is an anchor investor. Total fund $110M. Promotes financial inclusion through digital lending platforms.
recipient_organisation: Lendable Inc. / Lendable Fintech Credit Fund

financier: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands
scope_basis: Programme develops digital trade: e-commerce and digital services exports.
title: Develop Digital Trade Competitiveness In Selected African Countries
description: Programme to develop digital trade competitiveness of services sectors in selected African countries. Focuses on e-commerce, digital services exports, and trade facilitation in support of inclusive economic growth and AfCFTA.

scope_basis: Grant deploys digital health tools.
title: Digital Health for COVID-19
description: Support to the deployment of digital health tools for COVID-19 tools deployment in Sub-Saharan Africa

scope_basis: Regional infrastructure programme; digital networks are one strand beside transport and energy networks.
title: Investments on regional infrastructures
description: Development of resilient continental/inter-regional infrastructure for transport multimodal networks, energy networks and digital networks via blended finance, feasibility studies and support to Sub-Saharan African Transport Policy Program

scope_basis: Project strengthens digital economy statistics and data science use in tax and customs administrations.
title: DATAFID — Regional Project to Support Strengthening of Digital Economy Statistics and Use of Data Science by Tax and Customs Administrations
description: DATAFID aims to increase knowledge about the digital economy and its impacts, and to build the capacities of tax and customs administrations through improved use of data science. Two components: (1) improving knowledge of the digital economy to include it in the tax system; (2) improving the transparency and performance of tax and customs administrations. Beneficiary countries: Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire, Niger, Senegal, Togo (Component 1); Côte d'Ivoire, Mauritania, Niger, Togo (Component 2). Implemented with AFRISTAT, INSEE, FERDI. Financed by the French Directorate-General of the Treasury (DG Trésor) under the Strategic Investment Plan for Development (PISD) 2020–2023.
recipient_organisation: AFRISTAT; INSEE; FERDI; national tax and customs administrations

scope_basis: Programme entirely about digital access: connectivity, digital skills and digital inclusion regulation.
title: UK Digital Access Programme (DAP) — Multi-country
description: The Digital Access Programme (DAP) is a FCDO-DCMS joint programme catalysing more inclusive, affordable, safe and secure digital access for excluded and underserved communities in Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa, Brazil and Indonesia. Components include: (1) Support to inclusive connectivity, digital skills, content and services for underserved communities (delivered via KPMG-led consortium); (2) Technical assistance on policy, legal and regulatory frameworks for digital inclusion; (3) Programme management and advisory. Achieved reach of 10.2 million people across all five countries. Cybersecurity capacity building (Pillar 2) funded separately under Africa Cyber Programme. Commit and disbursement figures represent IATI-reported FCDO share, SSA-attributable portion (KE/NG/ZA = 3/5).
recipient_organisation: Governments/implementing partners in Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa (plus Brazil, Indonesia outside SSA)

scope_basis: Fund makes equity investments in African technology start-ups.
title: Google Africa Investment Fund — $50M Equity Fund
description: Google established the $50 million Africa Investment Fund at Google for Africa 2021 to make equity investments in early- and growth-stage African technology startups. The fund provides equity capital plus access to Google technology, employees, and networks. Initial portfolio (as of 2022): SafeBoda (Uganda, mobility super-app), Carry1st (South Africa, mobile gaming), Lori Systems (Kenya, logistics). Individual ticket sizes are not publicly disclosed.

description: Swedfund invested in Apis Growth Fund II, a continuation of Apis Growth Fund I targeting financial services and fintech companies providing digital financial services to underserved populations across Africa and South Asia. The fund focuses on mobile payment, savings, insurance and credit services. Fund II closed at USD 563 million hard cap in December 2019. Swedfund's prior commitment referenced as part of its ongoing Apis partnership since 2015.
recipient_organisation: Apis Growth Fund II (Apis Partners LLP)

scope_basis: Initiative to map schools and connect them to the internet.
title: Giga — School Connectivity Initiative for Sub-Saharan Africa (UNICEF-ITU Joint Programme)
description: UNICEF-ITU joint initiative launched in 2019 to connect every school to the internet and every young person to information, opportunity and choice. In SSA, Giga is active in 20+ countries including Kenya, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Niger, Zimbabwe, Benin, Botswana, Namibia, South Africa and Guinea, providing school mapping, connectivity planning, procurement support, and financing facilitation. By November 2023, Giga had mobilized >USD 47.6 million from 14 partners (Ericsson, Dubai Cares, Musk Foundation, SoftBank, BCG, IHS Towers, GSMA, Dell, FCDO, and others). UNICEF is the primary lead of the Giga initiative with ITU as co-lead. Activities include open-source school mapping (Project Connect), real-time connectivity monitoring, government procurement support, and innovative financing models including outcome bonds and connectivity credits. As of 2023, Giga had connected 14,500+ schools globally, benefiting 7.79 million students, with SSA countries (Kenya, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Botswana) accounting for a significant share.
recipient_organisation: Governments of Kenya, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Niger, Zimbabwe, Benin, Botswana, South Africa et al.

scope_basis: Digital financial services, digital skills and digital market development.
title: Digital Economy and Market Development (DEMD) Mechanism
description: USAID Digital Economy and Market Development mechanism supporting digital ecosystem development in Nigeria and Uganda. Covers digital financial services, digital skills, and digital market development.

scope_basis: Task order covers training, facilitation and digital services; the text does not say how much is digital.
title: GSA Training, Facilitation and Digital Services Task Order
description: USAID digital services task order covering training, facilitation and digital services across multiple SSA countries including Mozambique, Nigeria, Niger, Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, South Sudan.

scope_basis: Equity in a fibre network operator to expand its cable network.
title: Liquid Intelligent Technologies — Equity Investment (Fibre Network SSA)
description: BII invested $180M equity in Liquid Telecommunications Holding Limited in December 2018 to accelerate expansion of its fibre optic cable network across Sub-Saharan Africa (Cape-Cairo route and Central/West Africa). Liquid is the largest independent pan-African fibre network operator with over 100,000km of cable serving Kenya, Rwanda, DRC, South Africa, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Tanzania, Uganda, Nigeria, and others. Investment supports affordable broadband access for businesses and consumers. BII remains a shareholder in Cassava Technologies (parent company post-restructuring).
recipient_organisation: Liquid Telecommunications Holding Limited (now Liquid Intelligent Technologies / Cassava Technologies)

scope_basis: Commitment to a venture fund investing in tech-enabled businesses.
title: Novastar Ventures Africa Fund II — LP Commitment
description: BII committed $15M to Novastar Ventures Africa Fund II in October 2018. Novastar is a Nairobi-based venture capital firm specializing in early-stage tech-enabled consumer businesses in East and West Africa. Fund II expanded Novastar's geographic mandate to West Africa and invested in companies including Turaco (insurtech), Pula (digital crop insurance), and others leveraging technology for impact in underserved markets. BII is a significant anchor LP.

scope_basis: Initiative supports digital identity and civil registration systems.
title: Commonwealth Digital Identity
description: Commonwealth Digital Identity Initiative improving access to a digitally-enabled identity for every woman and girl in the Commonwealth by 2030. Partners with World Bank, GSMA and Caribou Digital to work with developing countries. Total value AUD 6.0 million over 2 years starting 2017-18. Commonwealth SSA members include Ghana, Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe, South Africa, Mozambique, Malawi and others. Activity supports foundational digital ID infrastructure and civil registration systems.
recipient_organisation: Commonwealth Secretariat / GSMA / World Bank / Caribou Digital

financier: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands
scope_basis: Partnership also covers investment and governance for private sector development, not only e-commerce and digital economy.
title: UNCTAD Strategic Partnership 2018-2021 E-Commerce And Digital Economy
description: Multiyear UNCTAD partnership on investment, e-commerce and digital economy, and governance for private sector development. Supports developing countries to benefit from digital economy growth, particularly LDCs in SSA.

scope_basis: Financing is for optical fibre roll-out.
title: EAST AND CENTRAL AFRICA OPTICAL FIBER ROLL OUT
description: Financing for optical fibre roll-out across East and Central Africa. Supports high-speed broadband deployment in underserved areas. EUR 54M EIB commitment.

scope_basis: Grants programme for scaling digital social innovations.
title: D4D Programme / WeHubit 1.0 — Digital Social Innovation Grants
description: Wehubit 1.0 (D4D Programme) implemented by Enabel and BIO on behalf of Belgian development cooperation. Supports scaling of digital social innovations (fintech, agritech, e-health, edtech, digital infrastructure) across 14 official Belgian partner countries in SSA. EUR 9.345M Enabel-managed budget; additional EUR 14M committed by BIO for private sector digitisation projects. Programme provided grants of EUR 50K–350K to 27+ digital social innovations across 13 Enabel partner countries.

scope_basis: Loan to a wholesale connectivity carrier for fibre and data centre expansion.
title: WIOCC Group — IFC Loan (2018)
description: IFC provided a $20 million senior loan to West Indian Ocean Cable Company Ltd. (WIOCC), a carrier-of-carriers offering wholesale connectivity to over 20 countries across Africa. WIOCC operates terrestrial and submarine fibre optic networks and data centres across Sub-Saharan Africa, supporting ICT infrastructure for internet service providers, mobile operators, and enterprises. The 2018 investment supports WIOCC's expansion of fibre networks and data centre capacity across the continent.
recipient_organisation: West Indian Ocean Cable Company Ltd. (WIOCC)

scope_basis: Spectrum policy, licensing and coordination for wireless broadband.
title: PRIDA Component 1: Policy and Regulation Initiative for Digital Africa - Spectrum Management
description: ITU-managed spectrum component of the AU-EU-ITU Policy and Regulation Initiative for Digital Africa (PRIDA). Aims to harmonize spectrum utilization across Africa to facilitate wireless broadband deployment. Activities: spectrum allocation policy based on international best practices; spectrum licensing and pricing frameworks; cross-border frequency coordination agreements; IoT awareness. EU-funded via Pan-African Programme. ITU contributes EUR 500K own funds. Covers all 54 African countries.

scope_basis: Loan finances a mobile operator's network upgrades and refinances its debt.
title: Africell Holding — OPIC $100M Telecom Expansion Loan
description: OPIC loan of $100 million to Africell Holding Limited to finance upgrades and expansion of 2G, 3G, and 4G mobile networks in The Gambia, Sierra Leone, Uganda, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Up to $40M may refinance existing debt. OPIC commitment letter signed November 2018; finance agreement concluded May 2019. Africell is a US-owned mobile operator and the first to receive DFC/OPIC financing. The facility supported over 12 million subscribers and provided affordable mobile voice and data services in frontier markets. Africell repaid the loan three years ahead of schedule in December 2024.

scope_basis: Equity in a mobile financial services fintech.
title: JUMO — Mobile Financial Services Platform Africa (First Proparco Fintech Investment)
description: USD 3 million equity investment in JUMO, a fintech startup offering mobile loans, savings, and financial services to unbanked populations in SSA via mobile phone networks. JUMO's platform uses digital credit scoring algorithms. Proparco's first investment in an African fintech. Operates in Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Ghana.

scope_basis: Activity supports digital financial inclusion, fintech and digital payment adoption.
title: Alliance for Digital and Financial Services Activity
description: USAID activity advancing digital and financial services, supporting digital financial inclusion, fintech ecosystem development, and digital payment adoption.

financier: Belgian Investment Company for Developing Countries
scope_basis: Financial inclusion fund investing in banks, insurers and non-bank lenders as well as fintech.
title: AfricInvest Financial Inclusion Vehicle (FIVE) — Pan-African Fintech/Finincl Fund
description: EUR 10M equity in AfricInvest Financial Inclusion Vehicle (FIVE), formerly AfricInvest Financial Sector Holding. An evergreen pan-African investment fund focused on financial inclusion across Africa. Initial strategy targeted established banks, insurers, and NBFIs; evolved to include fintech companies with digital financial services. BIO partner for 20+ years with AfricInvest, investing EUR 76M total across 9 AfricInvest funds.

financier: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands
scope_basis: Funds a mobile health insurance and payment platform.
title: Health Insurance Fund Care Pay Mobile Health Platform
description: Care Pay is a digital intermediary platform linking healthcare providers, insurers, and users in Africa. The platform enables mobile health insurance administration at minimal cost, scaling financial inclusion through mobile technology across Sub-Saharan Africa.

scope_basis: Equity in a venture fund targeting digital and technology start-ups.
title: PARTECH AFRICA VENTURE CAPITAL FUND I
description: EIB equity participation in Partech Africa Fund I, first Africa-focused VC fund by Partech. EUR 124M fund launched 2018. EIB committed EUR 10M. Targets digital and technology start-ups across Africa. Successfully deployed.

scope_basis: Programme develops mobile technology services for humanitarian response.
title: M4H — Mobile for Humanitarian: Exploring the Use of Mobile Technology to Provide Life-Enhancing Services during Humanitarian Response
description: Works with the mobile industry and humanitarian organisations to develop cost-effective, scalable solutions and business models for delivering life-enhancing services during disaster preparedness, humanitarian response and recovery. Includes access to information and connectivity via mobile, financial services, and mobile utility access. Africa and SSA countries are the primary delivery region, with work in DRC, Ethiopia, Kenya, Nigeria, Somalia, and South Sudan.
recipient_organisation: GSMA Mobile for Humanitarian / implementing humanitarian organisations

scope_basis: Programme producing and managing geospatial and demographic data.
title: Geo-Referenced Infrastructure and Demographic Data for Development (GRID3)
description: Improves collection, management, analysis and use of geospatial and demographic data to improve lives of the poorest in developing countries. Enables better understanding of population distribution and location of key infrastructure (roads, hospitals, schools, water points). Geospatial data platform supports government planning, census operations, vaccination campaigns, and humanitarian response. SSA primary partner countries include Nigeria, DRC, Zimbabwe, Zambia, Madagascar, Mozambique, South Sudan, and others.
recipient_organisation: Columbia University CIESIN; WorldPop; national statistical offices

scope_basis: Digital platform for citizen engagement and health data.
title: Technological Platform for Civic Engagement and Improved Health Systems
description: Improves health care systems for women and those most in need through a citizen engagement digital platform in Burkina Faso, Benin, and DRC. The platform enables digital reporting, community health data collection, and civic feedback mechanisms.

scope_basis: Facility finances pay-as-you-go solar home systems alongside digital credit.
title: M-KOPA Pay-As-You-Go Solar and Digital Credit Facility
description: Norfund USD 13 million debt commitment as part of USD 80 million syndicated facility (Stanbic Bank lead; CDC USD 20M, FMO USD 13M, Norfund USD 13M). M-KOPA provides pay-as-you-go solar home systems and digital mobile money credit to off-grid households in Kenya and Uganda. Financing backed by customer receivables paid over mobile money payment plans. Digital scope: IoT smart metering, mobile money payment rails, digital credit scoring.

scope_basis: Equity in a venture fund dedicated to technology-enabled start-ups.
title: TIDE Africa Fund I — Venture Capital for Digital Start-ups Sub-Saharan Africa
description: USD 5 million (EUR 4.3 million) equity commitment to TLcom Capital's TIDE Africa Fund, a venture capital fund dedicated to technology-enabled start-ups in Sub-Saharan Africa. Fund invests EUR 500K–EUR 10M per company at growth stage. Focus: mobile phone and digital applications that provide access to essential services (food security, energy, health, education, financial services). Total fund first close EUR 40M. PROPARCO's commitment enabled the fund's first closing.

scope_basis: Advocacy for digital payments.
title: UNCDF Better Than Cash Alliance (Digital Payments Advocacy)
description: UNCDF Better Than Cash Alliance (BTCA) 2017-2018, advocating for the transition from cash to responsible digital payments to advance financial inclusion. The alliance engages governments and the private sector on digital payment policy and adoption globally, with significant focus on sub-Saharan Africa.

scope_basis: Programme on mobile operator commitments to connectivity, digital inclusion and mobile money.
title: GSMA Mobile Industry Leadership (M4D) 2017-2021
description: GSMA Mobile Industry Leadership programme 2017-2021, supporting CEO engagement and private sector leadership on mobile for development and the SDGs. The programme catalyses mobile operator commitments to digital inclusion, connectivity and mobile money in developing countries including sub-Saharan Africa.

scope_basis: Training programme for ICT regulators on telecom policy and spectrum.
title: ITP 316 ICT Regulation - Policy and Practice (Spider & PTS)
description: ITP 316 ICT Regulation: Policy and Practice programme 2017-2024, implemented by SPIDER (Stockholm University) in partnership with PTS (Swedish Post and Telecom Authority). Provides training and capacity support to ICT regulators in 27 sub-Saharan African countries on telecom policy, spectrum management and broadband regulation.

scope_basis: Agreement exists to identify and scale digital approaches across fintech, ICT policy and digital health.
title: Digital Frontiers - USAID Center for Digital Development
description: Digital Frontiers is a $74.4 million seven-year (2017-2024) USAID cooperative agreement administered by DAI that works with USAID Bureaus and Missions to identify and scale digital approaches globally including Africa. Covers digital inclusion, fintech, ICT policy, DCCP, and digital health.

scope_basis: Loan builds mobile telecom networks to cover unserved rural communities.
title: RURAL TELECOM NETWORK EXPANSION (DRC AND CAMEROON)
description: Construction and installation of mobile telecom networks to extend coverage to rural communities of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Cameroon currently not served. Networks using frequency bands under revenue share agreements. By end 2018: coverage to over 3.6M people via 650 sites. Extends mobile population coverage from 75% to 80% in DRC and 85% to 95% in Cameroon.

scope_basis: Capacity building and certification in digital finance.
title: Digital Frontiers Institute (DFI) — Phases I and II
description: FCDO grant through FSD Africa to the Digital Frontiers Institute for capacity building in digital finance. Supports professionals in Sub-Saharan Africa and globally through digital finance certification programmes including the Certificate in Digital Money (CIDM) and Certified Digital Finance Practitioner (CDFP). Phase I and Phase II ran from 2016 to 2022. Builds regulatory and practitioner capacity for digital financial services ecosystems across SSA priority countries. Part of FCDO's support to financial sector deepening in Africa through FSD Africa.

scope_basis: Partnership wholly about mobile technology: connectivity, mobile money and mobile-enabled services.
title: M4D - Mobile for Development Strategic Partnership
description: DFID/FCDO strategic partnership with GSMA and its Mobile for Development initiative to identify and support innovative ways mobile phone technologies and networks can improve reach, delivery and affordability of services for poor people in Africa and Asia. Phases include mobile connectivity, mobile money for the poor, utility services (energy, water, agri), and emerging technology applications (AI, big data). Africa is the primary delivery region. Programme phases 2016-2029 cover mobile infrastructure, digital inclusion, and mobile innovation with 14M+ beneficiaries expected. Latest phase (2024-2029) extends digital connectivity and inclusion work across SSA.

scope_basis: Core support for affordable internet access and digital rights advocacy.
title: World Wide Web Foundation 2016-2022 (Internet Access and Rights)
description: World Wide Web Foundation core support 2016-2022 for internet access and digital rights advocacy. Promotes affordable internet access, digital inclusion and open internet policies globally with substantial focus on sub-Saharan Africa through the Web Foundation's Alliance for Affordable Internet (A4AI) and related advocacy work.

scope_basis: Initiative entirely for digital health tools, health information systems and interoperability.
title: The digital health initiative (Digital Square)
description: Digital Square is a USAID-funded initiative implemented by PATH that supports the adoption and scale of digital health tools across countries. Activities span 24+ SSA countries including Ethiopia, Kenya, Nigeria, Tanzania, Uganda, Mozambique, Malawi, Ghana, Senegal, Rwanda, and others. Supports health information systems, DHIS2, data interoperability, and digital health enabling environments.

scope_basis: Programme builds statistical capacity.
title: Multinational - Statistical Capacity Building Program for Managing for Development Results – Second Annual Work Plan
description: The Multinational Statistical Capacity Building Program for Managing for Development Results responds to the increasing data needs for measuring development results, including those relating to the green and inclusive growth agenda. The program covers RPG-eligible countries, selected SROs, STCs and ...

scope_basis: Financial-inclusion fund investing in credit, savings and insurance companies as well as payments infrastructure.
title: Apis Growth Fund I — LP Commitment (Fintech/Payments Africa & Asia)
description: BII committed $30M to Apis Growth Fund I in August 2015, managed by Apis Partners. The fund supports financial inclusion in Africa and South Asia by targeting mid-market companies in payments infrastructure, credit and savings, insurance, distribution, and service providers. Africa is a primary investment focus (estimated ~50% of portfolio). This is BII's first investment in Apis Partners, an anchor LP position that catalysed the fund to close at $287.5M.

scope_basis: Expands a digital skills and digital livelihoods programme for youth.
title: Digital Livelihoods: Youth and the Future of Work at Scale
description: Expands Digital Opportunity Trust (DOT) economic empowerment programming across SSA and MENA, building digital skills, social innovation, and entrepreneurship for youth including women and girls. SSA countries: GH, KE, MW, RW, SN, TZ, ZM (84% allocation).

scope_basis: Centre of excellence for civil registration and vital statistics systems.
title: Centre of Excellence for Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS) Systems
description: Supports the Global Financing Facility in building the Centre of Excellence for CRVS Systems, aiming to end preventable maternal and child deaths through strengthened civil registration and vital statistics. 50% SSA allocation (regions 298+798 split).

scope_basis: Equity in a telecoms tower company.
title: Helios Towers Africa — IFC Equity Investment (2015)
description: IFC made a $35 million equity investment in Helios Towers Africa Ltd in 2015, an independent tower company operating in Tanzania, DRC, Republic of Congo, Ghana, and other SSA markets. Helios Towers provides passive telecom infrastructure including towers, shelters, and power systems to mobile network operators. The investment supported expansion of the company's tower portfolio across Sub-Saharan Africa, enabling greater rural connectivity and lowering the cost of mobile network deployment. Helios Towers listed on the London Stock Exchange in 2019.

scope_basis: Multi-sector private equity fund; digital and fintech are a significant allocation among other sectors.
title: Helios Investors III L.P. — IFC LP Commitment
description: IFC committed $25 million as a limited partner in Helios Investors III L.P., a $1 billion private equity fund managed by Helios Investment Partners focused on Sub-Saharan Africa. The fund targets investments across multiple sectors with a significant allocation to digital infrastructure and technology-enabled businesses, including mobile money, fintech, and ICT. Helios III invested in companies such as Interswitch (Nigerian fintech), Tipco (Nigeria), and other technology-enabled businesses across SSA.
recipient_organisation: Helios Investment Partners / Helios Investors III L.P.

scope_basis: Loan to a mobile network operator for 3G/4G rollout and capacity upgrades.
title: Africell Mobile Network Operator Expansion
description: IFC provided a $35 million senior loan to Africell Holding, a mobile network operator active in The Gambia, Sierra Leone, DRC, and Uganda. The financing supports network expansion, capacity upgrades, and improved mobile data services in four SSA markets. Africell is a Lebanese-owned MNO providing affordable mobile connectivity to underserved populations across its operating markets. Proceeds finance 3G/4G network rollout and infrastructure improvements to support mobile internet access and digital financial services.

scope_basis: Core support to an alliance whose mandate is digital public goods and mobile-enabled development.
title: Digital Impact Alliance (DIAL) 2015-2020
description: Sida core support to the Digital Impact Alliance (DIAL) predecessor programme 2015-2020, which established the global Mobile Hub and Greentree agenda for mobile-enabled development. Programme advances digital public goods and inclusive technology solutions with substantial work in sub-Saharan Africa.

scope_basis: Programme's whole purpose is ICT capacity development, research and training.
title: SPIDER 2015-2019 (Swedish Programme for ICT in Developing Regions)
description: SPIDER (Swedish Programme for ICT in Developing Regions) at Stockholm University supports ICT capacity development in sub-Saharan Africa. SSA beneficiary countries include Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda and Zambia. The programme provides technical assistance, research support and training on ICT for development across multiple sectors.

scope_basis: Fund invests in financial services companies as well as fintech; its portfolio includes a small-business lender.
title: Apis Growth Fund I
description: Swedfund committed SEK 63 million to Apis Growth Fund I, a private equity fund managed by Apis Partners targeting financial services and fintech companies at the intersection of finance and technology in Africa and South Asia. The fund focuses on mobile payment services, savings, credit and insurance for underserved populations. Africa portfolio companies include Direct Pay Online (pan-Africa online payment platform) and MicroCred (pan-Africa mSME lender). First close August 2015; fund reached USD 287 million final close in 2017.
recipient_organisation: Apis Growth Fund I (Apis Partners LLP)
